title: Deliver the collaboration interface: account, workspace, membership, device and key initialization, sync state, conflict, and audit surfaces
story_count_note: Seventeen stories, CF-P7-001 through CF-P7-017. The count moved twice and both moves are recorded rather than smoothed over. The plan was frozen with fourteen. CF-P7-015 was added after the freeze and took the next free number, which is why the highest id has been ahead of the last story in sequence ever since. CF-P7-016 was added to fix a defect in a frozen Phase 7 contract that the Phase 8 plan found (R-P7-E), and CF-P7-017 was added to dispatch the API shell that has answered 503 on every route since Phase 1. Several documents once read '13 of 14'; that was wrong twice over -- wrong denominator and, once CF-P7-016 landed and CF-P7-017 was opened, wrong numerator too. CF-P7-014 corrected it to '13 of 15' on 2026-07-27 and to the present '14 of 17' in the same story once the two later stories existed. The count is a machine-readable field here and is checked against the exit manifest and against the exit report's own status line by cf:phase7:exit:check, so the next drift fails a gate instead of being read by eye. 'The original fourteen' in the CF-P7-015 reason below is historically correct and is deliberately left alone: the plan did hold fourteen stories before CF-P7-015 was added.
principle: Phase 7 adds no cryptographic, persistence, or authorization primitive. It is the interface over the Phase 3 to Phase 6 services. Every read and write goes through an existing service; the UI layer may not reimplement identity, envelope, revision, idempotency, cursor, membership, or outbox logic.

stories.reason: Phase 7 was planned as the interface over the Phase 3 to Phase 6 services, and every surface story was gated on performing no transport of its own. That held, and nothing was ever built on the other side of it: no module called /api/v1. CF-P7-013 found the consequence on Preview, where the entry rendered loading permanently because there was nothing to ask for a session. The layer is numbered after the original fourteen because it was added once the plan was already frozen, and sequenced before CF-P7-013 because CF-P7-013 cannot pass without it.

stories.title: Integrate and qualify the collaboration UI on Preview

requalification.result: PARTIAL -- unchanged, and for a reason that is now larger than it was
requalification.second_blocker_found: The owner set COLLABORATION_ENABLED='true' for the Pages Preview environment and D-P7-01 is executed in wrangler.jsonc, and the route still answers 503. The reason is in the shell, not the configuration: functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs lines 285-293 compute hasReviewedDisabledState and then return the same 503 COLLABORATION_UNAVAILABLE on BOTH branches. The value routes nothing. No value of COLLABORATION_ENABLED can make any /api/v1/* route answer anything else, so the owner action recorded in blocked_on is necessary and is no longer sufficient.
requalification.why_no_journey_is_qualified_now: Two independent reasons, either of which alone would be enough. First, every collaboration route answers 503 on every deployment, so there is no session, workspace, member, invitation, key envelope, or audit event in existence to qualify against. Second, and true even after CF-P7-017 lands, the journeys this story must qualify are signed-in journeys and no OAuth session is available to the agent running the qualification: sign-in requires entering credentials at github.com, which the permission classifier refuses, and no session cookie was issued to or held by this story. Qualifying CF-P7-013 is therefore an owner-driven exercise, not an agent-driven one.
requalification.not_claimed: Nothing about the on-path was measured. No 2xx response from any collaboration route has ever been observed by this programme on any deployment.
requalification.followup: CF-P7-017 landed 2026-07-27 (D-P7-02): the dispatch bug named above is fixed in the working tree. Not observed on a deployment -- no agent pushed a commit or triggered a new Preview build, and Cloudflare Pages binds code at build time. The no-agent-OAuth-session blocker is independent and unaffected.

measured_budget_breach.narrowest_reading_note: Excluding the three inherited Phase 5/6 service modules the lazy path also pulls (device-key-lifecycle.js 5,212 B, outbox.js 5,457 B, conflict-resolution.js 3,708 B), the seventeen Phase 7 modules alone are 65,872 B = 64.3 KiB gzip. There is no reading of 'the Phase 7 chunk' under which this passes.
measured_budget_breach.measured_on: Preview deployment 681ad3ca-f0f7-4f66-8649-c7dab3de798d, as Cloudflare serves it
measured_budget_breach.gated_by: cf:phase7:exit:check, built by CF-P7-014 on 2026-07-27. Until that date this key was read by no script under scripts/ and no gate computed a byte size of any collaboration module, which is why a budget declared at plan time was first measured at integration time.
measured_budget_breach.cause: There is no bundling or minification step. Twenty unminified source files are served with comments intact.
measured_budget_breach.status: OPEN -- neither met nor renegotiated. Recorded, not accepted.

local_measurement.method: gzip level 9 over each module of the entry's static import closure, with CRLF normalised to LF so the number is the same on a Windows working copy and in CI. This is a reproducible lower bound computed by the gate itself, not a substitute for the deployment measurement above.
local_measurement.note: Slightly above the 78.4 KiB measured on the deployment because gzip -9 differs from Cloudflare's dynamic compression and because CF-P7-016 added mappings to api-client.js after that measurement was taken. Both readings breach 60 KiB under both the twenty-module and the seventeen-module reading.

measured_budget_breach.disposition: RECORDED AS AN OPEN BREACH, owner-visible. Option (b) of the two available: the number was not amended and the modules were not shrunk.

options.option: Renegotiate the budget on the record
options.consequence: A Product Owner decision in docs/collaboration-foundation/decision-log.md raising lazy_phase_7_chunk_max_kib_gzip from 60 to a number the current shape meets, with the reason. Cheapest, and it concedes that the 60 was never derived from a measurement. The gate then enforces the new number instead of this record.

options.option: Add a build step and meet the declared 60
options.consequence: Minification and/or bundling of js/collaboration/*. It is the only route that makes the shipped bytes smaller rather than the target larger, and it is a change to how the whole app is built -- currently every file is served as authored. It needs its own story and its own gate, and it would invalidate the byte-for-byte artifact assertions Phase 1 built.

Load the eight panel surfaces on demand rather than through one entry closure, so the first collaboration payload is the chrome plus the client. Keeps the budget and the no-build property, at the cost of more dynamic imports and a second latency step the sprint's UX criteria never asked for.

What is recorded today. The breach stays visible in the exit report, in the risk register as R-P7-B, and in this manifest; cf:phase7:exit:check re-measures it on every run and fails if the record and the bytes disagree in either direction. It also keeps open_defect on the Phase 7 zero-tolerance list unsatisfied, which is one of the reasons P7-G5 is not granted.
options.requires: no decision -- this is the default and it blocks P7-G5

stories.title: Assemble Phase 7 exit and Phase 8 handoff
stories.reason: PASS as a story, which is not the same thing as Phase 7 closing. Everything this story owns is delivered: the exit report is complete and signed, the Phase 8 handoff is issued, cf:phase7:exit:check exists with its policy module, manifest and drift suite and is wired into check:cloudflare, CF-EV-P7-EXIT-001 is written, and the story arithmetic is corrected everywhere and is now machine-checked. What this story cannot do is grant P7-G5, and it does not: CF-P7-013 is PARTIAL, CF-P7-017 is OPEN, and the lazy-chunk budget is an open defect. Two things about the way it was done stay on the record rather than being tidied away. P7-G4A, this story's entry gate, was never reached, because CF-P7-013 never reached it; the work was done out of gate order under an explicit owner instruction. And its own gate is a reconciliation gate -- it proves the record is internally consistent and re-measures the budget, and it cannot prove a journey that nobody ran.

stories.title: Correct the frozen error-to-presentation map
stories.out_of_sequence_reason: It re-opens and re-closes P7-G1, the contract gate, long after P7-G1 was passed, so it does not sit anywhere in the linear chain. phase-8-sprint.md found the defect while enumerating what Phase 8 needed: phase-7-ui-contract.md section 4 claimed every code in the frozen server taxonomy maps to exactly one presentation and then mapped twelve of the twenty-nine in api-contract.md section 8, two of them under spellings no catalog contains. It was numbered as a Phase 7 story rather than a Phase 8 one precisely so a later phase does not edit a frozen contract and a closed phase's gate. Recorded as R-P7-E in the exit report before it landed.

stories.title: Dispatch the API shell when the collaboration flag is on, and keep refusing when it is off
stories.out_of_sequence_reason: It is a server story opened inside a UI phase, because CF-P7-013 cannot be qualified without it. It shares CF-P7-013's exit gate P7-G4A: neither story reaches that gate until both are done.
stories.boundary: Dispatch when the flag is on; keep answering 503 when it is off. Production is permanently in the second case, pinned by six assertions across four closed phases and by D-P7-01, which authorized activation for Preview only. A change that makes the on-path work but weakens the off-path is a failure, not a partial win.
stories.resolution: Option A chosen by the Product Owner, 2026-07-27, recorded as D-P7-02 in docs/collaboration-foundation/decision-log.md: environment.ts was the bug. Its condition was corrected to require COLLABORATION_ENABLED === 'true' to enable, matching D-P7-01's already-executed intent for Preview. api-shell.mjs's dead double-branch was removed in the same change, with no observable behaviour change. Five workers-test fixtures were updated from the old, inverted polarity, and an explicit on/off contrast test was added at both the unit and the runtime-dispatch level. See CF-EV-P7-OPS-006.
decision_taken: Option A -- treat functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts line 67 as the bug: fix the polarity so COLLABORATION_ENABLED === 'true' enables, align functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs line 286, and keep the preview-origin, APP_ENV === 'preview' and hasCollaborationDatabase guards as the containment for production. This activates the Phase 3 to Phase 6 stack on a publicly reachable preview alias and needs the owner to say yes explicitly.

Option B -- treat the Pages Preview environment variable as the bug: revert COLLABORATION_ENABLED to 'false' for Preview (owner-only; wrangler pages secret put and the dashboard are refused to agents), roll D-P7-01 back across the gate scripts and tests/api-shell.test.mjs, and record the reversal in docs/collaboration-foundation/decision-log.md.

gate_ux.criterion: Personal vault and workspace data are never mixed
gate_ux.required: no personal record is ever rendered on a workspace surface and no workspace record on a personal surface; zero personal writes originate from any collaboration path; zero collaboration modules are evaluated on personal startup

gate_ux.criterion: The user always knows which workspace they are in
gate_ux.required: the active workspace is identifiable on every collaboration surface without opening a menu, at every supported width, and it survives reload and back-navigation rather than silently defaulting

a control the current role may not use stays visible, is programmatically disabled rather than merely styled, and states the reason in text that assistive technology announces; it is never silently hidden and never fails only on submit

gate_ux.criterion: A local draft is never lost to a conflict
gate_ux.required: the local draft survives the conflict dialog being dismissed, navigation away, and a full reload; it is discarded only by an explicit confirmed choice, and no automatic merge is ever performed

gate_ux.criterion: Keyboard navigation and focus states meet the bar
gate_ux.required: every surface is completable by keyboard alone in a logical order, with a visible focus indicator meeting WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast, no focus trap, and focus moved and restored correctly around dialogs

gate_ux.criterion: Mobile and tablet layouts do not break
gate_ux.required: every surface renders without horizontal page scroll, overlapping controls, clipped text, or unreachable actions at 320 px width, tablet portrait, and tablet landscape, including long workspace and account names

quality_budgets.lazy_phase_7_chunk_budget_history: Renegotiated from 60 to 100 by D-P7-03 on 2026-07-28, with the measurement in front of the owner. The 60 was written at plan time and read by no script until cf:phase7:exit:check existed, so it was never derived from a measurement of anything; meeting it needs a bundling step this project does not have. 100 sits above the measured 91.93 KiB with roughly 8 KiB of headroom, which is deliberate: a budget set at the measurement is unfalsifiable, and one set far above it enforces nothing.
